description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives are: (i) to provide beneficiaries in selected municipalities with: (a) updated and integrated cadastral and property registry information; and (b) improved land administration services; and (ii) to provide immediate and effective response to an eligible emergency.

The development objective of the Property Rights Strengthening Project for Nicaragua is to provide beneficiaries in selected municipalities with: (a) updated and integrated cadastral and property registry information; and (b) improved land administration services. Project design reflects the progress achieved by Nicaragua over two phases of PRODEP implementation, emphasizing the need to ensure that the Project will help establish a functioning and sustainable land administration system, and sufficient capacity among the country's land agencies and municipalities to deal with remaining issues. Accordingly, Project design centers around three strategic themes: (i) fine-tuning the institutional and policy framework and integrating systems; (ii) expanding cadastral, regularization and titling services to the central region of the country; and (iii) strengthening of municipal capacities for land administration and territorial planning. The Project includes five Components. The first four Components are directly related to outcomes (a) and (b), while Component 5, consistent with the strategic approach taken for Nicaragua, corresponds to potential support for immediate emergency recovery. First component, institutional and policy framework and system integration will strengthen Nicaragua's land administration system by supporting key policy consolidation and inter-institutional coordination and collaboration, and furthering the integration of the cadastre and property registry information and streamlining of processes. Second component, castrate, regularization and titling services will support the production of cadastral information and the recording and clarifying of land rights through systematicand on-demand land regularization, including issuance of legal documents as well as new titles and their registration. The systematic process will continue to focus on beneficiaries belonging to the "reformed sector.” On-demand activities will focus on beneficiaries prioritized by government programs, including small producers not belonging to the reformed sector. Third component, municipal land administration services will strengthen land administration capacities at the municipal level to promote their effective performance in the national cadastral system, as well as the better use of information for local planning and fiscal purposes, disaster risk management and overall development. In the medium term, this Component will contribute to enhancing the impact of cadastral information and the sustainability of cadastral investments; Fourth component, project management, monitoring and evaluation will support PGR, and its PCU, to manage the Project and to monitor its progress and evaluate it; Fifth component, Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) reflecting the strategic approach taken in Nicaragua across the Bank's portfolio, this Component will provide immediate response to an eligible emergency. As such, in the event of such eligible emergency (as defined in the CERC Operational Manual already prepared and adopted by the government), and at the request of the government, the Component would finance emergency activities and expenditures through the reallocation of funds from the Project.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I.A.1. Establishment of the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) - The Recipient shall operate and maintain, at alltimes during Project implementation, the PCU, the Inter-institutional Committee (CIP), and the Operational Technical Committee(CTO)with a structure, functions, responsibilities and adequate resources, all satisfactory to the Association. The Recipient shallensure that the PCU shall include, as its core staff, a general coordinator and a technical coordinator, a procurement specialist,a financial management specialist, a monitoring and evaluation (M&E) specialist, a social/gender specialist, an environmentalspecialist, and a communication specialist, all with terms of reference, qualifications, and experience acceptable to theAssociation.

Schedule 2, Section I.B.2. Prior to the carrying out of any Project activity under Parts 2 and 3 of the Project in any givenSelected Municipality, the Recipient, through PGR, shall enter into an agreement (“Participation Agreement”) with each suchmunicipality, in coordination with the Nicaraguan Institute of Municipal Development (INIFOM), under terms and conditionssatisfactory to the Association, to address the roles of the Selected Municipalities within the Recipient's land administrationsystem, as further described in the Project's Operations Manual (POM).

Schedule 2, Section I.C.1. Safeguards Instruments. The Recipient, through PGR, shall carry out the Project in accordance with theprovisions of the Environmental Assessment (EA), the Environmental Management Plan (EMP), and the Process Framework, as applicable.The Recipient, through the PGR, shall not assign, amend, abrogate, or waive the EA, the EMP, the Process Framework, or anyprovision thereof, without prior approval of the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.C.2. The Recipient shall refrain from granting or considering any claims for lands within or adjacent toProtected Areas, unless said Protected Areas had been physically demarcated in a manner satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section IV.1. The Recipient, through PGR, shall: (a) have all the procurement records and documentation of the Projectaudited each calendar year during Project implementation, in accordance with appropriate procurement audit principles, byindependent auditors acceptable to the Association; (b) furnish to the Association as soon as available, but no later than sixmonths after the end of each calendar year, the procurement audit report of such audit by said auditors of such scope and in suchdetail as the Association shall reasonably request; and (c) furnish to the Association such other information concerning saidprocurement records and documentation and the procurement review thereof as the Association shall from time to time reasonablyrequest.

title.narrative: Geospatial information databases of INETER integrated under INETER's Spatial Data Infrastructure

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: The IDEC Geo portal's diagnostic, implementation plan and design have been completed.

title.narrative: Mediation agreements pre-qualified as potentially registrable that are formalized in the Property Register

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: 83 (out of 83) agreements were registered formally in the Property Registry, which shows 100% progress made in institutionalizing alternative conflict resolution. The conflicts were related to land parcel boundaries, inheritance rights, land donation rights, and access easement issues.

title.narrative: Effective resolution of grievances related to the project within an average period of five business days

comment.narrative: 111% achieved: From September 2019 to March 2024, the GRM received, attended, and resolved 6,831 cases documented and addressed by SE-PRODEP (100% resolved), of which 3,598 were filed by women (53%) and 3,233 by men (47%), regarding consultations (5,924), requests (881), complaints (17), and suggestions (9); with an average resolution time of 1.44 days per case. The topics were titling (61%), cadastral updating (15%), cadastral survey (14%), property disputes (5%), and others (5%). Regarding the communication sources, 4,946 were attended through the telephone lines (3,912 free toll-line + 1,034 other phone lines), 1,836 in the offices, and 49 by the field teams.

104% achieved: The gender strategy was measured through three variables: (i) Participation of women in social communication activities, (ii) Participation of women in public displays of cadastral information, and (iii) Women who benefit from new titles (jointly or alone).

title.narrative: Satisfactory independent evaluation of SIICAR in terms of operation, data, and security

comment.narrative: 106% achieved: SIICAR 2.0 reached its maximum development during the implementation of PRODEP III, becoming the core system of the SAT. According to the evaluation carried out by an independent consultant (within the framework of the Government's Final Project Evaluation), the results obtained were: highly satisfactory ratings in terms of safety (100%), operation (91.92%), and integration (94.98%), reaching an average result of 96%, exceeding the target (90%) by 6%, and the overall target by 16%.

title.narrative: Parcel-based data identified and linked in the cadastral and property registry modules of SIICAR

comment.narrative: 136% achieved: Using SIICAR 2.0, these two institutions identified and linked 458,303 parcels. The target was 50% or 337,790 parcels. And assuming a target of 100%, the project reached 68% (458,303 out of 675,579 parcels).

title.narrative: Legal documents issued to project beneficiaries

comment.narrative: 145% achieved: The population benefited from the issuance of 137,021 legal documents, exceeding the target of 94,500 documents (145%). Of this total, 115,713 were new titles (Target: 77,400), of which 58,800 titles, or 51 percent, were issued to women, either individually or jointly with their spouse, surpassing the 50 percent target (38,700). Issuing titles to women helped reduce inequality in property rights between men and women and constituted an important factor for their social and economic empowerment.

title.narrative: Parcels incorporated into the national cadastre database

comment.narrative: 149% achieved: Completion of cadastral surveying in 16 municipalities, with 146,515 parcels incorporated into the National Cadastre Database, of which 11,440 parcels were financed with the Nicaraguan Treasury's resources.

title.narrative: Municipalities with technical cadastre certified by INETER/INIFOM

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: Fifteen (out of fifteen) municipalities have been certified by INETER in cadastral maintenance and cadastral updating: 1) Rancho Grande, 2) Rio Blanco, 3) Boaco, 4) Teustepe, 5) Santa Lucia, 6) Comalapa, 7) El Coral, 8) El Castillo, 9) San Carlos, 10) San JosE de los Remates, 11) Camoapa, 12) San Lorenzo, 13) Juigalpa, 14) Santo Tomás, and 15) Acoyapa.

100% achieved: Municipal land diagnostics completed in fifteen (out of fifteen) municipalities: a) Department of Boaco: Boaco, Santa Lucia, San Lorenzo, and Teustepe; b) Department of Chontales: Juigalpa, La Libertad, Comalapa, El Coral, Acoyapa, Santo Tomás, and Villa Sandino; c) Department of Matagalpa: Rio Blanco and Rancho Grande; and d) Department of Rio San Juan: San Carlos and El Castillo.

title.narrative: Municipalities that incorporate at least 90% of INETER cadastral database into SISCAT

comment.narrative: 117% achieved: 21 (out of 18) Municipalities have incorporated at least 90% of the INETER cadastral database into SISCAT: Rancho Grande, Rio Blanco, San JosE de los Remates, Santa Lucia, Boaco, San Lorenzo, Teustepe, Acoyapa, Comalapa, El Coral, Juigalpa, Santo Tomas, Santo Domingo, San Carlos, El Castillo, Santa Maria, Macuelizo, Quilali, San Fernando, La Concordia, and Jinotega.

title.narrative: Municipalities that manage cadastral information with SISCAT linked to the national cadastre

comment.narrative: 117% achieved: The linking of SISCAT-SISCAF in 21 municipalities (target 18) has allowed the technical teams of the municipal cadastral to efficiently manage cadastral data and update the information of the National Cadaster, contributing to a better performance of the SAT at the national level: Rancho Grande, Rio Blanco, San JosE de los Remates, Santa Lucia, Boaco, San Lorenzo, Teustepe, Acoyapa, Comalapa, El Coral, Juigalpa, Santo Tomas, Santo Domingo, San Carlos, El Castillo, Santa Maria, Macuelizo, Quilali, San Fernando, La Concordia, and Jinotega.

title.narrative: Baseline, mid-term and final household impact evaluations

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: The M&E system was implemented as planned. The M&E Project staff conducted a baseline study for the PDO-level Indicator 3 and IRI 1.1. At the MTR and Final Evaluation, the GoN recruited several consultants to prepare both assessments: (1) SIICAR 2.0, (2) Environmental impact, (3) Gender Strategy, GRM, and Social Communication, (4) EFA, (5) Social impact, (6) Institutional Evaluation, (7) Response times for registration of real estate transactions in the property registries, (8) Gender Strategy Indicator, (9) Beneficiary satisfaction of cadastral and registry services through SIICAR 2.0, (10) Household survey - at closing, (11) Municipalities Evaluation, and (12) Evaluations' Coordinator. The Bank also supported the M&E team in linking each indicator with the allocated budget to measure each target's physical and financial achievement.

title.narrative: Updated and new technical manuals to establish and simplify institutional processes with a focus on gender equity

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: This indicator has been achieved (100%). The following Manuals have been updated under the project: 1) Cadastral Surveying (maintenance and updating), 2) Mediation of Property Conflicts, 3) Producer Titling Procedures, and 4) Demarcation of Protected Areas.
173% achieved: The cadastral survey has covered 752,598 hectares of the 435,671 planned.

title.narrative: Protected Areas that are demarcated and registered in the database of the National System of Environmental Infromation

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: Eight protected areas were demarcated (100% achieved): 1) Reserva Natural Cerro Musún, 2) Cerro Cumaica-Cerro Alegre, 3) Reserva Natural Mombachito La Vieja, 4) Reserva Natural Fila Masigue, 5) Reserva Natural Serranias de Amerrisque, 6) Refugio de Vida Silvestre Los Guatuzos, 7) ArchipiElago de Solentiname, and 8) Monumento Nacional Fortaleza El Castillo de la Inmaculada Concepción de Maria. The Communication strategy has been successfully implemented, raising awareness among the population to preserve the protected areas.

title.narrative: Reduction in number of days to complete recording of purchase/sale of a property in the Property Registers with SIICAR

comment.narrative: 208% achieved: This system helped improve services across the Property registry and Cadaster offices in the Project area. Improvements in services were corroborated by the substantial achievement related to the reduction in the number of days required to complete the recording of the purchase-sale of properties. This number went down from 25 days (target) to 12 days at project closing to complete the recording of purchases-sales of properties with SIICAR 2.0 (35 days: baseline).

title.narrative: Strategy and Business Plan for SIICAR completed and adopted by CSJ and INETER

comment.narrative: The strategy has been designed to be implemented after project closing, to be financed with national funds, and based on three aspects: (a) Budget management, (b) Institutional, technological, legal, and operational arrangements, and (c) Implementation. The strategy has been reviewed, approved, and signed by the PGR, the DNR of the CSJ, and INETER.

132% achieved: The new Integrated Cadastre and Registry Information System (SIICAR 2.0) was evaluated through a survey of a representative sample of SIICAR 2.0 users, demonstrating that SIICAR 2.0 is 99% satisfactory (by men and women users), and 99% by only women users.

title.narrative: Municipalities that use the tool linking SIICAR-SISCAT

comment.narrative: 167% achieved: The SIICAR 2.0-SISCAT linkage was established in Boaco, Ocotal, Esteli, San Carlos, and Juigalpa municipalities, achieving 167% (target: 3).

title.narrative: Mediations where land tenure conflict agreements were reached

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: Out of the 2,418 mediations conducted, 1,256 land tenure conflict resolution agreements were reached.

title.narrative: Lobster pots provided for economic recovery to artisan fishing communities

comment.narrative: 184% achieved: 1,445 lobster pots were provided for economic recovery to artisan fishing communities.

title.narrative: Time taken to implement the CERC

comment.narrative: 100% achieved: The CERC was activated on February 25, 2021, and concluded on August 25, 2022. Therefore, it was completed in the planned eighteen-month implementation period.
618% achieved: 1816 new fishing boats were purchased.
59% achieved: 263.94 kilometers (out of the 450 km. planned) for the rehabilitation of six rural road segments have been completed.

title.narrative: Productive kits provided for economic recovery to artisan fishing communities

comment.narrative: 226% achieved: 218 outboard marine motors of 4, 8, 15, 30, 40, 60, and 75 HP were delivered to fishing communities, and 173 beneficiaries received equipment and accessories for commercializing fishing products (scales, tables, knives, plastic baskets, and coolers). Beneficiaries of outboard marine motors are 70% men and 30% women, while fishing equipment and accessories beneficiaries are 8% men and 92% women.

73% achieved: The CERC benefited 62,396 people, of which 27,558 (44 percent) were women. Regarding rural roads, the CERC financed the rapid rehabilitation of six rural road segments for 263.94 km and benefited 60,438 people (26,593 women, 44 percent). And the artisanal fisheries sector directly benefited 1,958 indigenous people, including 748 women (38 percent) who received fishing kits, marine motors, fishing boats, and materials to build lobster pots.
